headline: At a San Francisco event, only three people said they would buy Anthropic shares at a $3 trillion valuation.
score_reason: Informal poll at one event plus IPO-market context; pool score 5 kept.
importance_line: It matters most to companies planning listings and to investors who would buy the shares, since the IPO market is thin beneath its headline numbers and Oura pulled its IPO last week, though the poll is one room's show of hands, not a market test.
summary: Business Insider reports that when its chief correspondent Ben Bergman asked a tech crowd at a Fidelity-sponsored event in San Francisco on Wednesday night whether it would buy Anthropic shares at a $3 trillion valuation, only three hands went up. Heidi Mayon, a partner at the law firm Simpson Thacher, said companies have been reluctant to list before Anthropic and OpenAI do, which makes Anthropic's public offering a test of how much AI hype survives public-market scrutiny.
notes: Read in full on Business Insider. The poll is an informal show of hands at one event. The article names an Anthropic investor who spoke onstage; not named here because the article gives no organisation for him.
